questionText: How do you implement idempotency for POST requests in Spring Boot?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can design a retry-safe Spring Boot POST using a scoped key, fingerprint, atomic reservation, durable replay record, and explicit failure rules.

claims.statement: POST is not idempotent by general HTTP method semantics, so a retry guarantee has to be defined by the individual API operation.
Spring Transactional metadata defines transaction semantics through Spring transaction infrastructure but does not itself make a check-then-insert sequence atomic.

examples.title: Transactional order service with an atomic reservation abstraction

validation.expected: The excerpt compiles against Java 17 and the selected Spring baseline once placed in a fixture

visuals.title: New, completed, processing, and mismatched key paths

notes: The sample repository method is intentionally an abstraction; its database implementation must enforce the unique atomic gate.
The operation-key header is presented as an API convention rather than an Internet Standard.
